claim: The LANDER is the process the source starts under the *START LANDERS banner: LANDST spawns a run of them. This is the arcade-marketing 'Lander' — Defender's base ground enemy, mapped in glossary.md.
Each lander is spawned as a scheduler process running the LANDS0 kidnap body: NEWP LANDS0,STYPE — an enemy IS a process (NEWP/STYPE), never its own tick.
A freshly spawned lander is placed two rows below the top of the play-field: LDA #YMIN+2 (then STA OY16,X on the next line) — the LANDER_SPAWN_Y constant in core/landers.ts.
The HUMANOID is the process under the *ASTRONAUT PROCESS banner (ASTRO): it walks the terrain. This is the arcade-marketing 'Humanoid', the abductee, mapped in glossary.md.

A carrying lander that reaches the top triggers the transform: FLEE tests the lander's Y against YMIN+8 (CMPA #YMIN+8) and, at or above it, falls through to LANDFX — the LANDER_TOP_Y trigger point in core/landers.ts (the mutant it becomes is df4-4).
Killing a lander that is CARRYING a humanoid drops the humanoid into a fall: LKIL1 (the swapped kill vector) starts an AFALL process. The banner *KILL KIDNAPPING LANDER marks this handler.
The dropped humanoid is launched as its own falling process: NEWP AFALL,STYPE START HIM FALLING — the shot-carrier -> AFALL chain.
AFALL accelerates the falling humanoid downward by 8 each tick: LDD #8 (comment ACCEL DOWNWARD), then ADDD OYV,X on the next line — the AFALL_ACCEL constant in core/landers.ts.
The fall speed is capped at $300: CMPD #$300 gates the accelerating velocity — the AFALL_MAX_FALL terminal-speed constant in core/landers.ts.
A grabbing lander tracks its target horizontally in $20 steps: LANDG loads LDB #-$20 (right-branch mirror LDB #$20 at :761) — the HUNT_X_STEP magnitude in core/landers.ts.
The humanoid (ASTRO) walks in $20 steps: ASTRX2 loads LDB #$20 for the walk-right move (left-branch mirror LDB #-$20 at :331) — the WALK_STEP magnitude in core/landers.ts.
LANDG3 'ARE WE ON HIM?' accepts a grab when the lander/target X distance is within $80: CMPD #$80 — the GRAB_X_TOL window in core/landers.ts.
LANDG3 aligns the lander within 12 rows of the target's Y before grabbing: SUBA #12 against OY16 — the GRAB_Y_TOL window in core/landers.ts.

The ASTRO humanoid turns around when the SEED byte is <= 8: CMPA #8 / BLS (walk-right mirror CMPA #$8 / BLS at :335) — the WALK_TURN_THRESHOLD in core/landers.ts (a SEED<=8 turn test, not a higher guessed value).

The lander's vertical velocity is LNDYV, a 2-byte RAM cell the df5 wave logic initialises: LNDYV RMB 2. df4-3 has no fixed ROM magnitude for descent/carry speed to port, so DESCEND_STEP/CARRY_STEP in core/landers.ts are disclosed df4-3 placeholders pending df5.

The MUTANT is the process the source starts under the *START SCHITZOS banner (SCZ / 'schizoid'). This is the arcade-marketing 'Mutant' — the enemy a Lander becomes on reaching the top, mapped in glossary.md.
Each schizoid is spawned as a scheduler process running the SCZ0 body: SCZS0 NEWP SCZ0,STYPE — the Mutant IS a process (NEWP/STYPE), never its own tick.

A carrying Lander that reaches the top transforms into a Mutant: SCZ00 DEC LNDCNT (INC SCZCNT on the next line) swaps one Lander for one schizoid — the lander->mutant transform df4-3's reachedTop trigger drives (transformLander in core/mutants.ts).
The Mutant process re-naps every 3 ticks: NAP 3,SCZ0 — the SCHIZO_NAP cadence in core/mutants.ts.
The BAITER is Williams' internal 'UFO' process: UFOST NEWP UFOLP,STYPE spawns it running the UFOLP body. This is the arcade-marketing 'Baiter', the timeout pursuer, mapped in glossary.md.
The UFO/Baiter process body is UFOLP, under the *UFO PROCESS banner: it seeks the player and shoots.
The Baiter's shot timer initialises to 8: LDA #8 (STA PD2,U INIT SHOT TIMER on the next line) — the UFO_SHOT_TIMER_INIT constant in core/ufo.ts, the first-shot delay.
The UFO/Baiter process re-naps every 6 ticks: NAP 6,UFOLP — the UFO_NAP cadence in core/ufo.ts.
The Baiter's velocity is the UFONV player-seek routine, under the *UFO VELOCITY banner: it aims the UFO's OXV/OYV toward the player (PLABX/PLAYC), with the vertical seek halved (ASRA, :76).

The Baiter is spawned on a TIMEOUT, not per-wave: the GEX002 countdown calls JSR UFOST when its timer expires (capped at 12 UFOs) — this is the 'timeout pursuer' the arcade calls the Baiter, sourcing the UFO->Baiter identity rather than assuming it.
The arcade-marketing name for the UFO process is spelled out in the message ROM: BAITER FCC "BAITER/" — the UFO->Baiter identity is SOURCED here, not an assumption (the story's own caution).

The BOMBER is Williams' internal 'TIE' process: the source banner *TIE PROCESS marks the formation flyer's body. This is the arcade-marketing 'Bomber' — the flyer that lays bombs — mapped in glossary.md (the story's AC1 guess of START BOMB->Bomber is corrected: the TIE is the Bomber, and BOMBST is the bomb it lays).

The TIE process DROPS BOMBS — this is the behavioral proof that the TIE is the arcade BOMBER: TIE31 gates on (LSEED & 7)==0 and, when open, BSR BOMBST lays a bomb (the 1/8 drop gate). BOMBST is the bomb/mine, not an enemy.
The bomber's process re-naps every tick: NAP 1,TIE — the TIE_NAP cadence in core/ties.ts.
The bomb-drop gate masks the LSEED byte with $7 (1-in-8): ANDA #$7 (BNE TIEX on the next line skips the drop unless the low 3 bits are zero) — the BOMB_DROP_MASK in core/ties.ts.
The number of live bombs is capped at 10: BOMBST loads BMBCNT and CMPA #10 / BHS refuses a new bomb at the cap — the BOMB_MAX in core/ties.ts.
A laid bomb's lifetime is (SEED & $1F) + 1: ANDA #$1F masks the seed (INCA on the next line adds one), so the lifetime is always at least 1 — the BOMB_LIFETIME_MASK in core/ties.ts.

The POD is Williams' internal 'PROBE' process: the source banner *PROBE START marks the drifting blob's spawn. This is the arcade-marketing 'Pod' — the 1000-pt blob that bursts into swarmers when shot — mapped in glossary.md (correcting the story's AC1 guess of PROBE->Probe).

Killing a PROBE RELEASES SWARMERS — the behavioral proof that the PROBE is the arcade POD: PRBKIL loads the count (LDA #6, :119) then JSR MMSW materializes 1..6 mini-swarmers at the pod's position before DEC PRBCNT.

A killed pod releases up to six swarmers: PRBKIL loads LDA #6 as the RMAX ceiling before JSR MMSW (RMAX returns 1..6, so a shot pod ALWAYS bursts into at least one swarmer) — the POD_SWARMER_MAX in core/probes.ts.

The SWARMER is Williams' internal 'MSWM' (mini swarmer): the source banner *MAKE A MINI SWARMER marks its spawn routine. This is the arcade-marketing 'Swarmer' — the fast pursuer a Pod bursts into — mapped in glossary.md (correcting the story's AC1 guess of MSWM->Pod).
The number of live swarmers is capped at 20: MMSW spawn tests CMPA #20 / BHI and refuses a new swarmer above the cap — the SWARMER_MAX (SWCNT cap) in core/swarmers.ts.
The swarmer process re-naps every 3 ticks: MSWL NAP 3,MSWLP — the SWARMER_NAP cadence in core/swarmers.ts.
The arcade-marketing name for the TIE process is spelled out in the message ROM: BOMBER FCC "BOMBER/" — the TIE->Bomber identity is SOURCED here from the marketing string, not assumed.
The arcade-marketing name for the PROBE process is spelled out in the message ROM: POD FCC " POD/" — the PROBE->Pod identity is SOURCED here from the marketing string, not assumed.
The arcade-marketing name for the MSWM process is spelled out in the message ROM: SWARMR FCC "SWARMER/" — the MSWM->Swarmer identity is SOURCED here from the marketing string, not assumed.

The humanoid ground row is the terrain-surface base offset $E0: BGALT sets ROFF = $E0 (LDA #$E0 SET BASE OFFSET) as the base the per-column altitude table walks from — the HUMANOID_GROUND_Y constant in core/landers.ts (= terrain.ts BASE_OFFSET) a rescued astro is deposited at. This is the flat terrain base, NOT the ASTS2 wave-spawn row and NOT written by the ROM's ALAND0 catch-resolve; df5-4 deposits here as a documented simplification of the ROM's per-column GETALT landing.
Clearing an astronaut decrements the live-humanoid count ASTCNT: ASTCLR ... DEC ASTCNT — the zero-transition the df5-4 panic edges on.

When ASTCNT reaches zero (the last humanoid lost) the planet explodes: the ASTCLR handler fires NEWP TERBLO,STYPE BLOW UP TERRAIN — the df5-4 panic trigger, presented via the df4-2 terrain-blow ADR-0005 policy.

GTARG returns EQ when no humanoid remains (LDA ASTCNT / BEQ GTX NOBODY LEFT), and a re-targeting lander that gets that EQ FREAKS into a mutant: LBEQ SCZ00 NO, FREAK — the df5-4 en-masse lander->mutant transform on the zero-humanoid panic.

The player catching a FALLING astronaut is the AKIL1 player-collision path (AKIL1 LDU OBJID,X ... branch on 'falling'), which spawns the P500 rescue pop-up — the df5-4 catch mechanic (the P500 VALUE is score.ts/df5-3).
